title: Classify a missing audio-provider key on a typed error, not on message text
body:
## Summary
POST /api/audio-gen decides 503-vs-502 by substring-matching the provider error message for "ELEVENLABS_API_KEY".

## Description
src/app/api/audio-gen/route.ts:143 `if (msg.includes('ELEVENLABS_API_KEY')) return apiError(msg, 503)`. The providers throw a plain Error with that text (src/lib/audio-gen/providers/elevenlabs.ts:57, src/lib/audio-gen/providers/elevenlabs-speech.ts:40). The error-handling golden path (software-engineering/backend-platform/resilience/error-handling, "Classify on structure, never on prose") says classification keys on a structured field; a reworded message silently turns "not configured" into a 502 "provider failed", and an upstream message that contains the env-var name becomes a 503. Fixed: providers throw a typed not-configured error (or one carrying a `code`) and the route branches on that.

## Flow
- provider throws `new Error("ElevenLabs key missing")` (a reword) -> route returns 502 instead of 503
- fix: add a typed error in src/lib/audio-gen/, throw it from both providers, route checks instanceof/code

## Expected impact
The Forge shows "not configured" vs "provider failed" correctly whatever the wording. Could break: a future provider relying on the substring.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the 503 survives a reworded provider message
Before: 1 classifier keyed on prose; walked reword case -> 502 (1 of 1)
After: typed error: 0 prose classifiers; reword case -> 503
Method: simulation - walked the reword case by reading; the fix spans src/lib/audio-gen/providers (outside this context)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: route test: vi.mock the provider registry with a provider throwing a typed not-configured error whose message lacks the env-var name; expect 503 (red today, green after). Never a live provider call.

title: Guard audio-scene row blobs like level-design does: one bad row 500s the list
body:
## Summary
src/lib/audio-scene-db.ts rowToDoc JSON.parses zones/emitters unguarded and never checks Array, unlike level-design-db parseBlob.

## Description
src/lib/audio-scene-db.ts:56-57 `zones: JSON.parse(row.zones || '[]')`. A corrupt or non-array blob (written before this round's route guard d35b4e14, or by another writer) makes GET /api/audio-scene throw for EVERY scene, and getAudioSceneSummary (src/lib/audio-scene-db.ts:132-144) iterates the value (emitters null -> TypeError on `emitter.type`). The twin src/lib/level-design-db.ts:50 parseBlob tolerates both and flags the doc broken - a pair where only one was fixed. Fixed: the same parseBlob shape in audio-scene-db.

## Flow
- seed an audio_scenes row with emitters = 'null' or zones = '{'
- GET /api/audio-scene -> throws -> 500 for the whole list
- fix: parseBlob-style guard in rowToDoc returning [] and marking the scene

## Expected impact
One damaged scene no longer hides every other scene in the designer. Could break: nothing reads the raw parse error.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the list GET survives one bad row
Before: seeded bad row -> list GET 500 (predicted from code)
After: list GET 200 with the bad scene flagged
Method: simulation - src/lib/audio-scene-db.ts is in the audio-scene-designer context, not this round
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/lib/audio-scene-db.ts:56
src/lib/audio-scene-db.ts:57
src/lib/audio-scene-db.ts:143
src/lib/level-design-db.ts:50-64 (the guarded twin)
instrument: test on a throwaway POF_DB_PATH: insert a row with emitters='null' via getDb(), call GET /api/audio-scene, expect 200 (red today)

title: Validate audio-scene PUT scalar fields before they reach the row
body:
## Summary
PUT /api/audio-scene forwards name, globalReverbPreset, soundPoolSize and maxConcurrentSounds unchecked into buildUpdateQuery.

## Description
After this round's d35b4e14 zones/emitters must be arrays, but the PUT in src/app/api/audio-scene/route.ts still passes `soundPoolSize: "lots"`, `globalReverbPreset: 42` or `name: {}` to updateAudioScene (src/lib/audio-scene-db.ts:104-113). SQLite stores them; rowToDoc casts them back and generateAudioCode emits them into generated C++. Fixed: name string, preset inside the reverb vocabulary (src/types/audio-scene.ts), pool sizes positive integers - 400 otherwise.

## Flow
- PUT {id, soundPoolSize:"lots"} -> 200, the row holds "lots"
- generateAudioCode writes it into the generated header
- fix: typed checks in the route + cases in src/__tests__/api/audio-scene-request-shape.test.ts

## Expected impact
Generated audio C++ cannot carry a non-numeric pool size. Could break: a UI sending numeric strings.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - bad scalar fields refused
Before: 0 of 4 scalar fields checked (read)
After: 4 of 4 checked, 400 on each bad value
Method: simulation - read the route; not built this round for budget
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: extend src/__tests__/api/audio-scene-request-shape.test.ts: soundPoolSize "lots", maxConcurrentSounds -1, globalReverbPreset 42, name {} -> expect 400

title: Lift the 11 inline JSON-object body readers into one api-utils helper
body:
## Summary
Eleven API routes now each carry their own copy of "parse JSON, refuse a non-object with 400"; nine of them were added by this round to stay inside its paths.

## Description
Copies: src/app/api/audio-scene/route.ts and src/app/api/level-design/route.ts (readObjectBody), src/app/api/audio-gen/route.ts (isJsonObject), inline in audio-codegen, spatial-audio-generate, animations/mixamo-result, procgen/zone-pins, pattern-library, audio/import-result; plus src/app/api/project-health/route.ts and src/app/api/ability-spec/codegen/route.ts; related shapes in src/app/api/pipeline-artifacts/_lib/sweepBody.ts and src/app/api/blender-mcp/_lib/body.ts. One helper `readJsonObject(req)` returning Result<Record<string, unknown>, Response> in src/lib/api-utils.ts makes the house shape one authority.

## Flow
- grep "Body must be a JSON object" src/app/api -> 11 files
- add readJsonObject to src/lib/api-utils.ts with its own test
- migrate the copies; src/__tests__/api/game-world-content-body-shape.test.ts stays green unchanged

## Expected impact
One place to change the refusal status/text. Could break: tests pinning a per-route message.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one implementation of the body-shape rule
Before: 11 inline copies (grep)
After: 1 helper, 0 inline copies
Method: probe - counted the copies; the helper belongs in src/lib/api-utils.ts, outside this context
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: grep -c "Body must be a JSON object": audio-codegen 1, audio-gen 2, audio-scene 2, level-design 2, pattern-library 1, project-health 1, spatial-audio-generate 1, ability-spec/codegen 1, animations/mixamo-result 1, audio/import-result 1, procgen/zone-pins 1
instrument: inline-copy grep count (11 -> 0) plus the existing body-shape suites green

title: Bound animation-ledger projectPath to a known UE project root
body:
## Summary
GET /api/animation-ledger reads any directory named in ?projectPath= that has a Content/ or Source/ child.

## Description
src/app/api/animation-ledger/route.ts:13-18 takes projectPath from the query and hands it to buildLedger, which walks that tree. Anything that can reach the dev server can enumerate an arbitrary directory's asset/code references. The app already knows its project root (projectStore / UE context). Restricting to known roots is an authorization choice: a local single-user tool may accept the exposure, which is why this is the operator's call.

## Flow
- GET /api/animation-ledger?projectPath=<another repo with Source/> -> a ledger of that tree
- option A: refuse unless it is a known project root; option B: keep and document it

## Expected impact
Narrows a read-anything-with-Source/ surface. Could break: CLI/MCP callers that pass other project roots.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - narrower filesystem read surface
Before: any path with Content/ or Source/ is readable
After: only known project roots
Method: simulation - read the route; whether the exposure matters is a policy decision
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
instrument: route test: projectPath outside the known roots -> 403, once the operator picks the rule
